about: Version history of jacksalici.com, reconstructed from the git history and rendered by src/components/VersionTimeline.astro on /notes/website.

scheme.major: x.0.0: the site is rebuilt, on a new framework or with a new structure. Shown with a large screenshot.
scheme.minor: x.y.0: a change of style (palette, type, layout), or a notable feature on the same base.
scheme.patch: Content, fixes and dependency updates. Not listed.

fields.date: Day the version reached the main branch.
fields.commit: Commit the screenshot was built from, usually the last one before the next version.
fields.screenshot: Homepage built from `commit` and captured in Chrome at 1440x900 (device scale 1.5), light colour scheme.

versions.title: Breadcrumbs and a portrait
versions.summary: A palette of four colours, breadcrumbs on every page, and papers turned into a research collection with their own lists and filters.
changes: Iconoir icons in place of Lucide; every button shares the same hover behaviour.
Breadcrumbs on every page, derived from the URL.
Papers renamed to a research collection; a kind filter over the lists; Projects and Activities index pages.
Four colours, nothing else: background, ink, grey and a red accent, with text above WCAG AA contrast in both themes.
A portrait in the homepage hero and a new grid for the apps.
A Contacts page, linked from the header.
Sound effects off by default.
This timeline, which replaces the changelog table of the README.

screenshot.alt: White homepage: the headline 'A digital craftsman who designs systems that matter.', a short bio, a tilted portrait photo on the right, and the news list below.

versions.title: One design system
versions.summary: The homepage drops the cards for a plain news list, and every page is rebuilt from the same few shared components with a single type scale.
changes: Minimal homepage: the news as a list, with a kind pill on each row.
Higher contrast, uniform page headers, a research page and a page for each activity.
Playground renamed to Apps; a simpler header.
Shared components (page header, section, list, grid, button, chip) and one type scale across pages.
Sound effects on the shared components, with a mute toggle in the header.
LaTeX in Markdown, through remark-math and rehype-katex.
Paper and project pages rewritten with figures and screenshots, plus scripts to export paper figures and to screenshot websites.

screenshot.alt: White homepage with a one-line headline, a two-paragraph bio, plain contact links and a news list with a kind pill on each row.

versions.title: Inter only, on Vercel
versions.summary: A typographic clean-up: Inter for everything, with Space Grotesk and Space Mono gone. Hosting moves from Netlify to Vercel.
changes: Minimal design set entirely in Inter.
Hosting moved from Netlify to Vercel.
Simple Analytics replaced by Vercel Web Analytics, still without cookies.

screenshot.alt: Light grey homepage in Inter: a large headline, a polaroid portrait and four grey activity cards.

versions.title: Minimal yet catchy
versions.summary: A new structure: a header with navigation and search, research activities as the backbone of the homepage, and a playful layer of sounds, haptics and a dark mode.
changes: New homepage built around activity cards, 'What I am doing right now', and a polaroid portrait.
A new activities collection grouping papers and projects; activity pages replaced by anchors on the homepage.
Site header with navigation, full-text search (Pagefind) and links to sections.
Redesigned playground of small web apps and toys.
Sound effects (cuelume) and haptic feedback (web-haptics).
Dark mode, with a toggle.
Images served as optimised derivatives through astro:assets.
Package manager moved from npm to Bun.

screenshot.alt: Light grey homepage with a header, the words 'systems that matter' in red italics, a polaroid portrait captioned 'Me @ ICCV25, Honolulu', a search field and four activity cards.

versions.title: Back to the light side
versions.summary: Back to a light theme, and a new structure: the homepage becomes a single filterable feed of notes, papers and projects.
changes: Light theme with a red accent.
Homepage as a news feed, with search, category and type filters, and sorting.
A one-line news summary for every entry.
Categories refactored and lower-cased; tags kept for SEO only; redirects for the old URLs.
Lucide icons.
Later in this version: Astro 6 (April 2026) and 7, and a map of the conferences where the papers were presented, drawn with MapLibre GL (June 2026).

screenshot.alt: Light homepage with 'digital craftsman' in red, a bio, and a list of notes, papers and projects under search and filter controls.

versions.title: The batman version
versions.summary: A black theme with glass chips, rebuilt on Tailwind CSS 4, plus a playground and a flea market.
changes: Black theme with glass-effect chips and a two-column homepage.
SCSS and the Tailwind 3 integration replaced by Tailwind CSS 4.
Space Grotesk, Space Mono and Inter, self-hosted through Fontsource.
A playground page for small web apps.
A flea market for things I sell.
A gallery component with a lightbox, coloured contacts, a better 404 page and a dropdown menu.

screenshot.alt: Black homepage in two columns: an ICLR 2026 news chip, the headline and two pill buttons on the left, the bio on the right.

versions.title: Systems that matter
versions.summary: New colours and a new homepage around the line 'A digital craftsman who designs systems that matter', with large link boxes and new index pages.
changes: New palette: light grey, with black and grey link boxes labelled in Space Mono.
Projects, Notes and Contacts pages; no footer on the homepage.
Ongoing projects highlighted.
Later in this version: the first papers and research activities as content collections (July 2025), then venue acronyms on the papers (August 2025).

screenshot.alt: Light grey homepage with the headline 'A digital craftsman who designs systems that matter.' and four large link boxes, two black and two grey, with monospaced labels.

versions.title: Bento
versions.summary: Back to a light theme: a homepage of rounded blocks in lavender, navy, yellow and pink, set in Space Grotesk and DM Sans.
changes: Homepage made of bento blocks.
New palette and new fonts, Space Grotesk and DM Sans, in place of Monaspace and Inter (May 2024).
Menu, footer, homepage and article template refined (September 2024).
Simple Analytics, without cookies (September 2024).
Plain Markdown pages, such as the gaze dataset page.

screenshot.alt: Lavender-white homepage made of rounded blocks: a navy headline 'Digital craftsman, creative engineer.', a bio block, a yellow 'Check out my projects!' block and a pink 'Contact me!' block.

versions.title: Astro
versions.summary: Rebuilt from scratch with Astro, for three reasons: it is UI-agnostic, it is component-based from top to bottom, and it is faster than Hugo (+3% on PageSpeed Insights).
changes: Hugo replaced by Astro; posts and projects moved to typed content collections.
Dark navy theme with a gradient rule under the hero.
Monaspace and Inter fonts, and all icons, self-hosted.
No external scripts: Google Analytics removed.
Better SEO metadata, a facts page, a theme-color meta tag and a 404 page with an easter egg.

screenshot.alt: Dark navy homepage with the headline 'Digital craftsman, creative developer.', a monospaced bio, social icons and a rainbow gradient rule.

versions.title: Covers
versions.summary: Thumbnails for posts and projects, on the homepage and in the lists.
changes: Cover images for posts and projects.
Salinger theme updated to match.

screenshot.alt: Light homepage with the serif headline 'Digital craftsman, creative developer.' and a list of highlighted projects, each with a thumbnail.

versions.title: Tailwind and DaisyUI
versions.summary: A complete rebuild of both this site and the Salinger theme with Tailwind CSS and DaisyUI. The theme goes back to its own repository, used here as a git submodule; it was one of the themes featured at the 2023 Hugo Convention.
changes: Salinger rewritten with Tailwind CSS and DaisyUI and added back as a submodule.
Selectable DaisyUI colour themes, with a toggle in the menu.
Newsreader headings with Ubuntu and Ubuntu Mono text.
Material Symbols as inline SVG icons; Twemoji for the same emoji on every system.
Table of contents, a hero partial, and taxonomies for categories, languages and tools.
Google Analytics 4; Netlify configuration pinned to Hugo 0.112.
A facts page.

screenshot.alt: Light grey hero with the serif headline 'Digital craftsman, creative developer.', a monospaced bio and social icons, above a list of highlighted projects.

versions.title: Less is more
versions.summary: A new palette and no more special effects, for the sake of minimalism.
changes: Black background with sand-coloured headings.
Rotating circular tagline, random-letter title and contact box removed.

screenshot.alt: Black homepage with the sand-coloured headline 'People call me Jack.', a monospaced bio, social icons and a featured project card.

versions.title: Theme-less Hugo
versions.summary: The theme folder goes away and the layouts live in the site itself. A navy and sand palette, a tagline that turns on a circle, and a contact form on Netlify.
changes: Hugo theming removed: layouts and assets moved into the project.
Dotted navy background, sand headings in Climate Crisis, text in Roboto Mono.
Tagline set on a circle with CircleType; random-letter animation on the title.
Contact form on Netlify Forms with client-side validation; hosting moved from GitHub Pages to Netlify (March 2023).
Table of contents, 404 and privacy pages, tags and keywords.
Reveal-on-scroll animations with IntersectionObserver.

screenshot.alt: Navy dotted homepage: the sand headline 'People call me Jack.' over a blue tagline, 'Creative developer, digital craftsman', set on a circle.

versions.title: Dark dots
versions.summary: A dark blue dotted homepage, with a hover effect on the dots.
changes: Dark blue background with a dot grid and an SVG hover effect.
Tagline running vertically along the left edge.
Merriweather Sans and Roboto Mono.
New navbar and footer; projects tagged by programming language.

screenshot.alt: Dark blue dotted homepage with a small centred logo, one line of text and social icons; the tagline runs vertically along the left edge.

versions.title: Morning gradient
versions.summary: Salinger gives way to a custom theme, first prototyped in plain HTML and SCSS: a landing homepage on a cream to light blue gradient.
changes: Custom Hugo theme, prototyped as a static HTML and SCSS page.
Landing homepage: logo, one line and social links over a giant translucent tagline.
Montserrat throughout; Twemoji for consistent emoji.

screenshot.alt: Homepage on a gradient from blue to cream, with a small centred logo and social icons over a giant translucent tagline, 'Creative developer & digital craftsman'.

versions.title: Howdy
versions.summary: A restyle of the Salinger theme: a serif headline, emoji everywhere, social icons and a navigation bar.
changes: Libre Baskerville headings next to Montserrat.
An emoji-rich introduction and social links.
A header linking the projects and a new contact page.
Sections turned into categories; tags.

screenshot.alt: White homepage with the large serif headline 'Howdy, people call me Jack.', an emoji-filled bio, social icons and a list of recent projects.

versions.title: Hugo and Salinger
versions.summary: The first version tracked in git: a static site generated by Hugo with Salinger, a theme I wrote and published on its own, deployed to GitHub Pages. Anything older was never versioned and is lost.
changes: Hugo static site, with the Salinger theme as a git submodule.
Built and deployed to GitHub Pages by a GitHub Actions workflow.
Google Analytics.
Custom domain, jacksalici.com (January 2022).
Montserrat headings and a list of the latest projects on the homepage.

screenshot.alt: White homepage with the bold headline 'Howdy, I'm Jack.' followed by pizza, cactus and laptop emoji, a short bio and a list of the last projects.
